Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?","### What the OSM‑based OpenMapTiles style looks for

They draw the badge with an **`icon-image`** that is built from two feature properties:

If any of those IDs are **missing from the sprite JSON** the layer falls back to drawing only the `text-field` (the number), which is exactly the “bare floating number” you are seeing.
## How to get the badges back **without touching the style layers**
You have three practical ways to make those sprite images available. All of them keep the existing layer definitions untouched.
### 1. Point the style at a sprite that already contains the needed images
The **official OpenMapTiles sprite** ships with the full set of US shield images. Use it (or a copy you host yourself) as the style’s `sprite` base URL.
*If you are already using a custom sprite for your own icons, switch to the **array form** (MapLibre GL JS ≥ 3.0) and keep both sheets:*
Now the shield layers resolve their `icon-image` as `default:us-interstate_2`, `default:road_3`, etc., and the badges appear automatically.
### 2. Add the missing images at **runtime** with `map.addImage`
If you cannot change the `sprite` URL (e.g. you are on a CDN that you cannot edit) you can **register the missing images on the fly**. Do it once after the map has loaded:
// Helper to load a PNG/WebP (or an SVG via an )
const img = await map.loadImage(url);          // returns {data: ImageBitmap}
map.addImage(id, img.data, opts);              // opts can include {sdf: false}
// Example – add the three US‑interstate badge sizes
// …repeat for us-highway_*, us-state_*, road_* as needed
Because `addImage` stores the image under the **exact same ID** the style expects, the existing `icon-image` expressions start working instantly—no layer edits required.

> **Tip:** If you already have a sprite sheet (PNG + JSON) that contains the missing icons, you can extract the individual PNGs from the atlas (e.g. with `spritezero`’s `extract` command) and feed them to `addImage`. This avoids rebuilding a whole new sprite.
### 3. Build a **combined sprite** that merges your custom icons with the OpenMapTiles shield sheet
If you prefer a single sprite request (fewer HTTP round‑trips) you can:
2. **Add** your own icons (or any extra badge sizes) to the same directory.
3. Run a sprite‑building tool (e.g. `spritezero`, `spreet`, or the **Martin** CLI) to produce a new atlas and JSON.
4. Host the new files and point the style’s `sprite` (or the array form) at the new base URL.
Because the original shield IDs are preserved, the style continues to work unchanged, and your extra icons are now available under whatever IDs you gave them.
